what_its_for: Maralixibat is used to treat cholestatic pruritus (severe itching caused by liver disease) in patients with Alagille syndrome, which is a rare genetic condition that affects the liver. It works by blocking a protein in the gut that normally reabsorbs bile acids, which helps reduce the build-up of bile acids in the body that causes the itching.
how_to_take: Take maralixibat by mouth as a liquid solution. Use the special oral syringe that comes with the medication to measure your dose carefully. Take it once daily in the morning, at least 30 minutes before your first meal of the day. Rinse the oral syringe with water after each use. Do not mix the medication into food or drinks.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose based on your child's weight. The usual starting dose is 190 micrograms per kilogram of body weight once daily. Your doctor may increase the dose after a few weeks if needed, up to a maximum of 380 micrograms per kilogram per day. Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly and never change the dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store maralixibat in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep it in the original bottle with the cap tightly closed. Do not freeze it. After opening, use the bottle within 60 days. Keep out of reach of children. Protect from light.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking other medications that contain bile acid sequestrants (such as cholestyramine or colestipol) at the same time as maralixibat, as they may reduce how well it works. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before starting any new medicines, vitamins, or supplements. Avoid grapefruit or grapefruit juice unless your doctor says it is okay.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you or your child experiences: severe stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, or extreme tiredness; unusual weight loss or poor growth; blood in the stool or black, tarry stools; or if itching gets significantly worse or does not improve after a few weeks of treatment.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in itching within the first few weeks of treatment, but it may take several months to see the full benefit. Keep giving the medication as directed even if improvement seems slow. Talk to your doctor if you are concerned about how well it is working.
special_populations: This medication is approved for use in children 1 year of age and older with Alagille syndrome. The dose is based on the child's body weight. Safety and effectiveness in adults or children under 1 year have not been fully established. Tell your doctor if your child has any other liver or kidney problems, as this may affect dosing. There is limited information on use during pregnancy or breastfeeding, so discuss all risks with your doctor.
